title: kern_mega DOS support, parking, residency; kern_dos
summary: The park is among the best-engineered code in the tree. The snapshot returns twice, like setjmp. It parks only the kilobytes in use, which works because the claim map is out of band. Its facts arrive by two independent routes, the launch block below 1MB and the header above it, and the stub cross-checks them. The parked kernel builds the stub itself, one macro defines the sum for both of its takers, and %if assertions pin the layout. kern_dos matches that discipline: one disk layer and one DOS core across two hosts, a self-checking launch-block wire format, DOS=HIGH trampolines that put one word on the program's stack, and an EXEPACK unpacker that walks the stream dry before writing anything. The defects are at the edges and mostly on recovery paths that rarely run. The stub's second integrity check, written for W7's case, can never run for a park. The HMA kern_dos's mouse vector leaves its A20 trampoline at the first poll. W7's A20 opening tests the gate once, after the anchor is already cleared. The snapshot's fallback can, in a narrow case, build a park below the 128KB floor that keeps the stage clear of the loader. Size: about 1,000 bytes of the live resume (measured spans in the low image: kd_resume's body, kd_extents and the 459-byte hbs_stub) are dead in both kern_mega kern_dos images, which is 1KB back to low-DOS programs (KD_IMG_KB 37 -> 36), and a 512-byte gate-only buffer sits in every shipped kern_dos's .bss. On the documentation side, the t_mirror guard the comments rely on does not scan kerndos/. SPEC 87.9 still describes a retired resume route, and several comments describe a hibernate path through the park stub that no longer exists.

strengths.title: The snapshot returns twice
strengths.evidence: kernel/megados.inc:735 mega_dosparkf; mega_dwake jmp mega_dosparkf.ret; snapshot point at :1018-1024
strengths.why: It is kern_big's hbm_wake pattern carried into protected mode. hbm_dosrun stays one straight-line routine with an `or al,al` in it, not a state machine. It is the model for any future suspend.

strengths.title: The trip's facts come by two independent routes
strengths.evidence: kerndos/kdpark.inc:106-110 passes the sum, KB and base from the launch block; kernel/megapark.inc:54-63 compares them with the header cells
strengths.why: A stray write that shrinks the header cannot restore too little and still agree with itself. The header is deliberately not summed, and the reason is written down at megados.inc:45-48.

strengths.title: The stub is the parked kernel's own build
strengths.evidence: kernel/megados.inc:1495 mega_dstubup copies mpk_stub out of HIBER.DRV's image
strengths.why: A kern_dos and a kernel from different commits only have to agree on two numbers, KDP_GDT and selector 08h, so versions cannot skew.

strengths.title: One sum macro, two takers
strengths.evidence: kernel/megados.inc:121-134 MPK_SUMLINES, used by mega_dsumall and megapark .sum
strengths.why: The 22-byte phase step and phase 0 at every window let the two chunk the regions differently and still agree. It is WEAVE-SPEC 1.2's source-sharing rule applied to an algorithm.

strengths.title: The runs park
strengths.evidence: kernel/megados.inc:592 mega_dmapb; SPEC 96.40.9 measures 196KB parked of 639KB
strengths.why: The out-of-band claim map makes free heap stateless, so only in-use KB are parked and the program still gets the whole of conventional memory. It is a reason never to put headers inside heap blocks.

strengths.title: mega_dacc
strengths.why: Setting every accessed bit before the sum removes the whole class of 'the CPU wrote a table I sum' failures for the price of one pass.

strengths.title: W7's anchor is cleared before anything is decided
strengths.why: A recovery that fails is never tried twice.

strengths.title: The launch block is a real wire format
strengths.evidence: kerndos/kdlaunch.inc: KDL_MAGIC/KDL_VER/KDL_TLEN, the KDL_FIELDS gather/scatter, the zero-means-unfilled convention
strengths.why: The sender counts the length and the receiver recomputes it from its own copy of one list. A table walk on each side replaces two copies of marshalling code, and absent fields read as defaults, not as zeros. It is better than DOS's EXEC parameter block.

strengths.title: One disk layer and one DOS core, two hosts, gated
strengths.evidence: kerndos/kdos.asm includes apps/dos/dos.asm and kernel/disk*.inc unchanged; kdshim.inc lists every stub with its section; t_kdfar.py and t_kdapi.py
strengths.why: The near/far hazard and the stray OSAPI far call, the two classic hazards of including code in a foreign root, are build failures.

strengths.title: DOS=HIGH trampolines with a private stack
strengths.why: MS-DOS 5's design, with better stack discipline: one FLAGS word on the caller's stack, so a program that shrank its block to its own SP keeps its MCB intact.

strengths.title: kd_xunp checks everything before writing anything
strengths.evidence: kerndos/kdxpack.inc:39-44 and the kxp_walk dry pass
strengths.why: A refusal leaves the image byte-identical, which is what makes the LOADFIX and kd_tolow fallbacks safe to chain.

strengths.title: The live resume's refusal discipline
strengths.why: Every refusal falls back to int 19h, nothing is torn down until the last moment, and the last message prints before the extent list is staged so a BIOS scroll cannot move it.

findings.title: The park stub's PCHK check can never run, and its mega_hbwake leg is dead
findings.detail: `cmp ax, mega_dwake / je .cells` jumps every PARK past `.cells0`. `.cells0` compares MPK_C_PKB and MPK_C_PBASE against the summed copy at MPK_SAVE, and its comment calls it the guard for 'a header shrunk in BOTH places - W7's probe has no other copy to pass'. It is reached only for wake = mega_hbwake. That never happens: mega_dhcfill's only caller passes mega_dwake, and the hibernate resume now runs through megares.inc's own tail. mega_wrprobe passes the header's own cells, so the first check compares the header with itself, and MPK_C_PKB (3B8h) is not summed. After a warm reset, a park whose PKB cell was damaged passes every check, and the restore then moves too little or runs past 640KB.
evidence: kernel/megados.inc:1363-1364 the only mega_dhcfill call, with mega_dwake
kernel/megares.inc:579 and kernel/hiber.inc:4469 the resume's own mrt_wake
kernel/megados.inc:2141-2149, 2229-2231 W7 passes the header's own cells
findings.recommendation: Route mega_dwake to .cells0 and delete the mega_hbwake compare and the NREG==0 arm. A park always has NREG>0, and MPK_SAVE and the header cells come from the same mega_dpkb and mega_dpbase, so a normal trip still passes.
findings.bytes_est: -12 HIBER.DRV image (cmp/je pair 5, NREG test 7), 0 resident
findings.verify_note: Re-read megapark.inc:67-88: mega_dwake takes `je .cells`, only mega_hbwake reaches .cells0. grep: the only mega_dhcfill call is megados.inc:1363 with AX = mega_dwake; mega_hbwake is written only into megares.inc's mrt_wake (hiber.inc:4469). W7 (megados.inc:2141-2149, 2229-2231) passes the header's own PSUM/PKB, and the sum starts at MPK_MAGIC (+400h), so MPK_C_PKB at 3B8h is unsummed while MPS_PCHK's copy at MPK_SAVE is summed. Not in ABI-BREAK-LIST or KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE. Byte estimate refined to -12.

findings.title: The HMA kern_dos's mouse vector leaves its A20 trampoline at the first poll
findings.detail: kd_mou_arm writes CS:kd_mou_isr (CS = FFFFh on the HMA arm). kdh_tramp then rewrites it to a LOW_SEG slot. kd_mou_rearm runs on every INT 33h AX=3 and every key poll (through kd_mou_read) and compares the vector against CS:kd_mou_isr, so the slot fails the test. It re-arms once: the vector becomes FFFF:kd_mou_isr with no trampoline, the UART is re-initialised and one RBR byte is drained, possibly mid-packet. From then on, a program that shuts A20 (a direct int 15h AH=87h, which kdx_i15 passes to an IBM-AT ROM that leaves A20 shut, or AX=2400h) takes its next mouse IRQ into wrapped low memory.
evidence: kerndos/kdmouse.inc:155-156 the vector written as CS:kd_mou_isr
apps/dos/dos.asm:3741 dos_hvec, the core's publish-through-slot helper (DOS_MEGA only)
findings.recommendation: On KD_HMA, publish the vector through kdh_vslot in kd_mou_arm and compare against the same answer in kd_mou_rearm (kdh_vslot hands back the existing slot for the same target). dos_hvec is %ifdef DOS_MEGA and so absent from kern_big's kern_dos: use it only under KD_MEGA (the low arm's dos_hslot = 0 answers CS:target) or call kdh_vslot directly under %ifdef KD_HMA, so kern_big's image is unchanged.
findings.bytes_est: +8 HMA kern_dos image only (HMA bytes, not the program's); 0 elsewhere if gated
findings.verify_note: Confirmed the defect: kd_mou_arm (kdmouse.inc:149-156) runs from kd_mou_start (kdentry.inc:327) before kdh_tramp (:396), which rewrites every IVT entry naming KD_SEG = FFFFh to a LOW_SEG slot; kd_mou_rearm (:391-395) then sees the slot and re-arms to FFFF:kd_mou_isr, after which the compare passes for good. kdx_i15 forwards AH=87h to the ROM (kdxms.inc:153, 186-187). Corrected the recommendation: dos_hvec exists only under DOS_MEGA (dos.asm:3734-3751, Makefile:7603 adds -DDOS_MEGA only for KERN_MEGA), so the reviewer's 'other arms behave as today' is true of the low mega arm but the call would not assemble on kern_big's kern_dos.

findings.title: W7's A20 opening tests the gate once, after the anchor is already cleared
findings.detail: mega_wrprobe clears the anchor, writes port 92h and then 8042 D1h/DFh. Its .kbw waits only for IBF to clear, which happens when the 8042 has read the byte, not when it has switched the output port. It then tests A20 exactly once and on a miss boots normally. The anchor is gone by then, so the session is lost with no message. The anchor read used int 15h AH=87h, which on an IBM-AT ROM leaves A20 shut, so the 8042 path is live on exactly the 286 ATs W7 targets. Every other opener in the area polls: kdh_tchk up to 65,536 times, kdp_a20w and mr_a20 512 times.
findings.recommendation: Poll the test (xor cx,cx / loop), as kdh_tchk does.
findings.verify_note: Re-read megados.inc:2105-2182: the anchor is zeroed and written back (:2112-2125) before the header is even read, then 92h, D1h/DFh with .kbw (IBF-clear only, :2235-2242), one compare of 0:FFE0 against FFFF:FFF0 and `jne .out`. kdh_tchk_src (kdhma.inc:224-228) loops 65,536 times after the same writes. Clearing first is deliberate (a failed recovery is not retried), which is exactly why a single premature test loses the session.

findings.title: The snapshot's fallback can build a prefix park below MPK_MIN_KB
findings.detail: The runs claim is KB-in-use + 16 with no floor. If the snapshot's recount outgrows it, .fallb parks a prefix of [mega_dclkb] KB, which can be under 128KB. The .ptry loop enforces MPK_MIN_KB, and megados.inc:94-97 says that floor is what keeps the stage (P - 16KB) clear of the loader's working area, with the packed kern_dos stream at KDS_TMPSEG = 64KB and up. The stage then sits at the OLD KB-in-use count, so it overlaps the stream only when that count was under roughly 64KB plus the packed stream's length, and the session's claims grew by more than 16KB between the claim and the snapshot. On kern_mega the kernel alone is ~70KB from 0600h, with LOW_SEG and DOS.O88's own claims above it, so the window is narrow.
evidence: kernel/megados.inc:1823-1840 mega_dstgs, the stage at P-16KB
findings.recommendation: Clamp the runs claim to at least MPK_MIN_KB in mega_dosclaimf.
findings.verify_note: The code path is real: .fallb (megados.inc:795-798) sets mega_dpkb = mega_dclkb = KB-in-use + MPK_SLACK with no MPK_MIN_KB test, and mega_dstgs (:1830-1839) puts the stage at dpkb*64 - 400h when drmode = 0. Severity lowered medium -> low: it needs >16KB of new claims between mega_dosclaimf and the snapshot AND an old in-use count low enough that (count) KB falls inside KDS_TMPSEG's packed stream; with a ~70KB resident kernel at 0600h plus LOW_SEG and DOS.O88 that is a narrow case.

findings.title: t_mirror does not scan kerndos/, so the kernel-to-kern_dos mirrors are unwatched
findings.detail: t_mirror scans a hand-written list plus kernel/*.inc and no kerndos/ file. Yet kdlayout.inc and hiber.inc (twice) name t_mirror as the guard, and megados.inc calls its KDL tail MIRRORED. The constants that cross between two artefacts on different disks are exactly the unwatched ones: KDL_CAP, KDL_XBASE..KDL_SNAPHI, KDB_*, KD_LSEG, KD_H_LBP/LBSZ and KDL_FLAGS. KDP_GDT (kdpark.inc) mirrors MPK_GDT under a different name, so even a glob would not compare them.
evidence: tests/unit/t_mirror.py:89-178 the ASM list, 343-344 KERNEL_GLOB only
findings.recommendation: Add kerndos/*.inc and kdos.asm to the scan, with DIVERGENT rows (and their reasons) for the arm-dependent KD_SEG, KD_ORG and KDL_VMAX. Rename KDP_GDT to MPK_GDT.
findings.verify_note: t_mirror.py main() builds its file set from ASM + glob(kernel/*.inc) + kernel/kernel.asm (:343-344); grep finds no 'kerndos' in the file. No other test compares them: tools/os88geom.py carries KD_SEG from hiber.inc only, and t_kdapi.py scans images for far calls, not constants.

findings.title: Both kern_mega kern_dos images carry the live resume they can never run
findings.detail: On KD_MEGA, kd_resume starts with `jmp .no`, but its body, kd_extents, the strings, the kdr_* bss and the hbs_stub (hbstub.inc) are all still assembled. Only kd_stageseg is reached, from kd_unpark. Measured in a scratch re-assembly of the low image (byte-identical to build/megak/kerndosl.bin): kd_resume 0x5E5F..0x5FC4 = 357 bytes, kd_extents to the end of kdresume.inc's own code 0x5FDB..0x6098 = 189, hbs_stub 0x6098..0x6263 = 459, and 23 bytes of kdr_* .bss. The LOW image's rung is off the DOS program: 37,510 of 37,888 measured.
evidence: kerndos/kdlayout.inc:148-154 the low arm's KD_IMG_KB 37 measurement
findings.recommendation: Gate the body, kd_extents, the strings, the kdr bss and the hbstub include under %ifndef KD_MEGA, keeping `kd_resume: stc/ret` and kd_stageseg. Then measure: predicted KD_IMG_KB 37 -> 36 on the low arm (37,510 - ~1,025 = ~36,485 of 36,864), +1KB per program there.
findings.bytes_est: about -1,025 each kern_mega kern_dos image (1,003 .text + 23 .bss, measured on the low arm); 0 on kern_big
findings.verify_note: Confirmed and re-measured: assembled kerndos/kdos.asm with the Makefile's kerndosl flags into the scratchpad (cmp identical to build/megak/kerndosl.bin) and read the listing. No label in kdresume.inc other than kd_resume, kd_stageseg and the DOSR_MARK-only kdr_mark_init is named outside it. Estimate raised from ~950 to ~1,025 bytes (hbs_stub is 459 there, not 441).

findings.title: kd_glb, a 512-byte gate-only buffer, sits in every shipped kern_dos's .bss
findings.detail: kd_glb is reserved unconditionally, but only kdosgate.inc, under KD_GATE, uses it. .bss counts against KIMG_SIZE and so against the rung, which is off the DOS program on kern_big and on the low arm.
findings.recommendation: Move it inside %ifdef KD_GATE.
findings.bytes_est: -512 rung (.bss) on kern_big's and both kern_mega kern_dos
findings.verify_note: kd_glb (kdentry.inc:1119-1121, resb KDL_SIZE = 512) is unconditional; every reference outside comments is in kdosgate.inc, whose body is %ifdef KD_GATE; kd_entry's bss clear keys off [kd_lbp], which shipped images point at kd_lblock, so removing it changes nothing at run time. On kern_big's shipped arm (34,796 of 34,816) it buys no whole KB by itself; on the low arm it combines with md-6.

findings.title: KDL_PLOW is written, documented as binding, and read by nobody
findings.detail: mega_dosgo stores PLOW and kdlaunch says kern_dos's arena must end below it, but no kerndos file reads it. KDL_CAP, lowered in the same branch, is what bounds the arena, and the two always agree.
findings.recommendation: Drop the stores and free the word, or reuse it for md-15's header sum. Fix the comment either way. The %if at megados.inc:163 names KDL_PLOW - KDL_XBASE as the copy run's length and keeps its meaning.
findings.bytes_est: about -15 .mega (two stores and the shl), or reused
findings.verify_note: grep: KDL_PLOW appears only in megados.inc (equ, the run-length %if, two stores) and kdlaunch.inc's equ; no kerndos/, apps/, tools/ or tests/ reader.

findings.title: mega_d8042get can bank a keystroke as the 8042 command byte
findings.detail: It flushes, sends 20h and takes the first non-AUX byte, accepting it if SYS (bit 2) is set. A scancode arriving in that window with bit 2 set (1Ch, 1Dh and about half of all codes) is banked. If its bit 0 is clear, mega_d8042put restores IRQ1 disabled and AEh does not undo that, so the keyboard is dead after the trip.
findings.recommendation: Send ADh before 20h and AEh after, or also require bit 0.
findings.verify_note: mega_d8042get (megados.inc:1944-1959) tests only bit 2; mega_dkobf skips AUX bytes but takes any keyboard byte; mega_d8042put writes the banked byte with 60h and then only AEh/F4h, neither of which sets command-byte bit 0. The window is a few microseconds with IF = 0, hence low.

findings.title: kd_unpark and mr_a20 wait only 512 probes for an 8042 A20 gate
findings.detail: kdh_tchk polls up to 65,536 times; 512 probes on a fast 386 is around a millisecond. On a miss, kd_unpark prints the A20 sentence and int 19h follows (W7 may rescue the park, if md-3 is fixed), and the streaming resume fails outright.
findings.recommendation: Use xor cx,cx in both.
findings.verify_note: Both loops are `mov cx, 512` around a ~25-instruction probe (kdpark.inc:135-142, megares.inc:480-486); kdh_tchk_src uses `xor cx, cx` (kdhma.inc:224). 'Under a millisecond' softened to 'around a millisecond' - the probe's own cost depends on the CPU.

findings.title: The park stub's 'press a key' accepts a PS/2 mouse byte
findings.detail: The refusal's key wait treats any byte with bit 7 clear as a key and never tests AUX (status bit 5). A mouse a DOS program left streaming restarts the machine on the first nudge, before the user has read the sentence. megares.inc already solves this with A7h.
evidence: kernel/megares.inc:252-256 the A7h fix (out 64h, A7h at :255)
findings.recommendation: Skip AUX bytes (test al,0x20), as mega_dkobf does, or send A7h first.
findings.verify_note: megapark.inc:242-254 tests status bit 0 and data bit 7 only; mega_dkobf (megados.inc:2002-2016) and megares.inc's .key (A7h) both handle AUX.

findings.title: mega_dreg_add silently drops a region on overflow
findings.detail: A full list drops the region, which then goes unsummed. Today's bound (MX_NBLK-2 blocks, one split, plus ~10 fixed regions, against MPK_RMAX = MX_NBLK+10) is held only by arithmetic in a comment.
findings.recommendation: Add an %if that states the worst case, so a new fixed region fails the build rather than the sum.
findings.verify_note: mega_dreg_add's .full path (megados.inc:484-485) skips the store with no flag. Counted the snapshot's fixed regions: image, HMA save, in-place rest, five table pieces, .cold/.mega, the header list = 10, plus pool blocks less park and arena with at most one snap split = MX_NBLK - 1; the bound holds today.

findings.title: Ten kdback.inc doors are call X / ret around routines with the same contract
findings.detail: dos_k_read, rdat, write, append, wrat, delete, mkdir, rmdir, rename and dfree wrap near targets with identical contracts. kdb_betab can name the targets directly (or the doors become equ aliases). The far, ES-sensitive and AL-sensitive doors keep their bodies.
findings.recommendation: Name the near targets in kdb_betab, or alias the doors with equ so any other reference still assembles.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: each of the ten is `call <near dskw_*>` / `ret` (4 bytes) and is reached only through kdb_betab -> dos_bevec in kern_dos.

findings.title: mem_free_x is a no-op behind a compare, and its comment says otherwise
findings.detail: Both paths `ret` without returning room; only kd_shed ever gives room back. The header says the most recent claim returns room.
findings.recommendation: Alias it to kd_nothing and correct the comment.
findings.verify_note: kdshim.inc:442-447 is cmp/jne/ret/ret (8 bytes); kd_nothing exists at kdshim.inc:184.

findings.title: Check the park header before jumping into it
findings.detail: The stub and its GDT run unverified. The kernel could put a 16-bit sum of header [0, MPK_C_END) into the freed KDL_PLOW word, and kd_unpark could read the header down with its existing kdx_87 and check it before lgdt. A mismatch takes the A20-failure path, so W7 still gets a try. The row changing meaning is a KDL_VER 6->7 bump on kern_mega's arm only.
evidence: kernel/megados.inc:45-48 the header is unsummed by design
findings.recommendation: Take it with md-8. The deeper variant: a 30-byte bootstrap that verifies the stub against HIBER.DRV's summed copy before running the rest.
findings.verify_note: Low-severity design proposal; not re-derived.

findings.title: mem_claim_x's overflow test is the last bit shifted out
findings.detail: `shl ax,cl / jc` with CL = 6 sets CF from bit 10 of the input only, so 2,560KB becomes 8000h paragraphs with CF = 0. No caller asks for more than a few KB today.
findings.recommendation: Add `cmp ax,0x400 / jae .no` before the shift, or comment the bound.
findings.verify_note: kdshim.inc:409-412: `mov cl, 6 / shl ax, cl / jc .no`; on the 8086 a multi-bit shift leaves CF = the last bit out (input bit 10). Latent only.

findings.title: The stub's restore loop is wrong when PKB < 33
findings.detail: Each chunk's byte count subtracts bp's place in its 32KB, which is right only when every chunk after the first starts on a 32KB boundary. With PKB < 33 the first chunk ends at (PKB-1)KB, mid-32KB, so the next pass's `sub cx, ax` subtracts a large offset from 1KB and CX wraps: the stub moves tens of KB past P (PKB = 20 moves ~46KB more; PKB = 2 moves 0 bytes and spins). MPK_MIN_KB and a runs park's kernel-holding first run keep PKB far above that.
findings.recommendation: Record. Comment it (or assert PKB >= 33 where the floor is set) if anyone lowers the floor.
findings.verify_note: Traced .rst (megapark.inc:176-198): bp=500h gives AX=1, CX=PKB-1; for PKB<33 the first move ends at (PKB-1)KB, then the second pass computes 1024 - (bp & 7FFFh) which wraps. So it overruns or hangs rather than 'restores PKB-1 KB'. Unreachable today (PKB >= 128 on a prefix park; a runs park's first run spans the ~70KB kernel), hence still 'record'.

findings.title: The trip's own time is not counted, and x87 state is not reset
findings.detail: The copy, sum and stub restore all run with IF=0. KDL_TICK is read after the park and the stub restores before hbm_wake reads the tick, so the clock catch-up misses milliseconds to half a second (MEGADIAG's DOSP line measures it). mega_dwake restores the MSW but not the x87 control word a DOS program left. Packages fninit per operation, so none is exposed today.
findings.recommendation: Record. If a package ever keeps x87 state across a yield, add FNINIT (gated on an FPU) in mega_dwake.
findings.verify_note: Record-only; not re-derived.

findings.title: HIBER.DRV-only scratch is resident in kern_mega's conventional .text
findings.detail: mega_hbxl, hbxd, hbs, hbr, hbbl and hbf are 22 bytes of conventional .text used only by the module's hbm_xwrite and hbm_xres. The park's MPS scratch above 1MB is the precedent, MPS_NAME and MPS_TKB having moved there in size pass 2. mega_hbwk (4 bytes) must stay: it is stamped before the picture so that it is IN the image, and mega_hbwake reads it after the image is back, while the MPS scratch is the fresh kernel's and not part of any image.
findings.recommendation: Move the six to MPS_* offsets; each site gains an ES override. Leave mega_hbwk in .text.
findings.verify_note: kernel.map has the seven cells at 4C66h-4C7Fh = 26 bytes, not 30. mega_hbwk cannot move: megados.inc:236-252 says the MPS tail 'is NOT SUMMED' and 'Nothing in it outlives one trip or one image', and hiber.inc:3946 stamps mega_hbwk before the picture precisely so mega_hbwake's `jmp far [mega_hbwk]` (megados.inc:1815) reads the image's value.

findings.title: KDLF_RAHSH is a shift count named like a flag bit
findings.detail: KDLF_RAHSH equ 8 sits beside KDLF_NOMOUSE equ 8 (bit 3). A reader checking for bit collisions trips on it.
findings.recommendation: Rename it KDL_RAHSH (three files).
findings.verify_note: kdlaunch.inc:356 KDLF_NOMOUSE equ 8 and :392 KDLF_RAHSH equ 8 (a shift for KDLF_RAHM 0700h); used as `mov cl, KDLF_RAHSH` in kdentry.inc and dos.asm.

findings.title: The A20 code is written out six times with four different budgets
findings.detail: The copies are mega_wrprobe inline (1 test), kdp_a20t/w and kd_a20shut (512), kdh_tchk_src (65,536), mr_a20 (512) and mega.inc's mega_a20. They live in four segments and three load contexts, so they cannot share a body, but they can share a macro for the test and the sequence.
findings.recommendation: Add an A20 macro on MPK_SUMLINES' precedent, so the budget is one number.
findings.verify_note: The individual budgets were checked under md-3 and md-10; the macro proposal itself not re-derived.

findings.title: kdlayout.inc is a changelog with a definition file inside it
findings.detail: 274 lines for about 30 definitions. The prose carries superseded measurements (wave 4's 45,827, the 61->43->34 history) and one truncated sentence, and it drifts.
findings.recommendation: Keep the current measurement per arm and the rule, and move the history into SPEC 96.44's measurement log.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: the truncated sentence is at kdlayout.inc:135 ('which holds 63' with no end) and the 61 -> 43 -> 34 history is in the KD_IMG_KB comment block (:180-200).

findings.title: Sum density per region class
findings.detail: The 1/32 sparse sum is right for pool blocks, which can be megabytes. For the kernel's own GDT, LDT, IDT and .cold/.mega, a few KB where a single wild word is most plausible, it catches an isolated changed word only about 1 time in 32. A per-region stride, dense there and sparse over pool blocks, costs about 10 bytes per taker. The XMS door and the AH=87h/88h filter already close the well-behaved routes.
findings.recommendation: Record. Revisit only if a field trip is ever refused without a cause.
findings.verify_note: Record-only design note; not re-derived.

findings.title: Reorganise the launch block at the next KDL_VER bump
findings.detail: The header has no spare byte, and the tail is a union by build (KDL_HOFF/HWDS/HSUM share bytes with XBASE/XKB). Every recent field was squeezed into a reserve that happened to exist (RSVD, HBPAD, POUT, MRSV). When the next field arrives: a header with 16 reserved bytes, the body, and a per-kernel tail named by a flag.
findings.recommendation: Take it at the next KDL_VER bump. It is a kernel/DOS.O88 version, not PKG_FMT.
findings.verify_note: Flag-day proposal; not re-derived.

findings.title: DOS 5 patched known EXEPACK stubs, and os8088 unpacks in the loader
findings.detail: MS-DOS 5's EXEC recognised the buggy EXEPACK unpacker and patched it, which is smaller. kd_xunp (~800 HMA bytes) unpacks any variant it can validate, keeping the 621KB arena. Since kd_tolow now runs refused programs on the low image with their own unpacker, kd_xunp buys ~36KB of arena per packed program and nothing else.
findings.recommendation: Keep. Recorded so the trade is explicit.
findings.prior_art: MS-DOS 5 EXEC's EXEPACK fix-up, plus LOADFIX
findings.verify_note: Record-only; not re-derived.

doc_fixes.old_text:
; **THERE IS NOTHING TO GO BACK TO ON THIS ARM**, which is the first
; deliberately destructive thing this OS does and reads like one: the user is
; to be asked in its own window, at the moment of launch, with Cancel as the
; default - docs/plans/KERN-DOS-PLAN.md §9, which is W7 and is not built. So
; the machine restarts - and it says so first, because a
; screen that goes black on its own is a crash and a screen that says why is a
; machine doing what it was told.
;
; W6's arm hangs off the same byte: with KDLF_REBOOT clear there is a
; hibernation image to put back, and this is where the return stub goes.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; HOME BY THE FIRST WAY THAT WORKS: a kern_mega park (`kd_unpark`), the live
; resume (`kd_resume`, SPEC.md 96.49), or `int 19h` with the exit code in the
; BDA (`kd_bda`, SPEC.md 96.41) for os8088's own boot to find. With no image
; at all (SPEC.md 96.42, where the user was asked first) the machine restarts
; - and it says so first, because a screen that goes black on its own is a
; crash and a screen that says why is a machine doing what it was told.
;
; Only a block with KDLF_REBOOT clear and no park reaches `.hold`, which has
; nowhere to go and says so.
doc_fixes.why: kd_leave jumps to kd_unpark when KDL_PBASE is set (kdentry.inc:815-820), calls kd_resume (:824), then int 19h via kd_bda when KDLF_REBOOT is set; the user is asked first per SPEC.md 96.42.
